observable_outcome: A Requirement can reach the only status the scheduler calls schedulable, and an Increment that goes into progress carries its parent with it. Measured at 76cfa91, neither is possible: domain.RequirementReadyCommand's sole non-test issuer is Service.AnswerHumanInput (internal/application/human_input.go:648), so ready is reachable only by asking a question and answering it; start, wait, recover, evaluate, pause and cancel have NO non-test issuer at all; and the only code that drives a whole journey, internal/runner/orchestrator.go:41-116, carries an Increment through Plan, Prepare, Claim and Start while the parent stays at captured -- and its only caller is a test. This task delivers the two edges the product documents license and STOPS, with a measurement, at the five they refuse or block. Edge one: Service.CompleteFraming in internal/application/framing.go issues ready from framing -- owner or scheduler, idempotent by request_id, gated by domain.Permit with kind claim, nothing passed to EffectFromPermit, no outbox item -- over POST /v1/requirements/{requirement_id}:complete-framing. Edge two: inside Service.Claim's existing transaction, when the claimed Increment's parent Requirement is ready, the start transition is issued from the version read in that same transaction, because docs/architecture/domain-model.md:266 DEFINES active as 'one or more Increments in progress'; when the parent is already active nothing happens. Completion is untouched: domain-model.md:101 says an Increment succeeding does not auto-complete its Requirement. What fixes the outcome is the chain asserted in one run over the composed handler -- capture, start-framing, complete-framing, plan, prepare, claim, parent active, second claim leaves it active -- plus the owner-driven half asserted against the real control-plane binary and the real Firestore emulator, plus the new command's seven-mode table. The reachable status set becomes exactly {captured, framing, needs-input, ready, active}.
